title: Adaptive choke-and-heal autoapply for batching/cache profiles
creator: Maya Chen
description: Goal: Implement an adaptive 'choke-and-heal' auto-apply controller that can safely roll out Optimize's batching and KV-prefix caching recommendations with automatic throttling and fast, observable rollbacks. This ticket covers controller design, canary policy implementation, operator approval hooks, and the runtime guardrails required for production-safe automated activation of cost-saving configs. The choke-and-heal model will gradually increase adoption while monitoring a small number of safety signals; if a signal exceeds thresholds the controller will 'choke' (pause and revert incremental steps) and run a healing sequence (rollback to last-known-good config, notify operators, run diagnostics). The system must support: scheduled windowed ramp-ups, percentage-based traffic ramp, simulated traffic dry-run mode, and integration with Console dashboards and Alerting channels.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Controller can take a recommended config bundle (batch_size, batching_timeout_ms, prefix_cache_ttl, cache_key_strategy) and apply it to a tenant via staged ramp (0% -> N% -> 100%) with operator-visible checkpoints. 2) Canary traffic run detects regressions against defined telemetry (p95 latency, server_error_rate, token_throughput, prompt-quality delta) and pauses/rolls back automatically when thresholds are breached. 3) Human approval flow (Console or API) can pause/resume rollout at any checkpoint; approval events are recorded in audit logs. 4) Rollback is fast (<30s to revert runtime routes to prior profile) and safe (no leftover cache corruption). 5) End-to-end tests and a simulated dry-run produce expected telemetry patterns. 6) Documentation and runbook for on-call are published under confluence.redwood.com/optimize/choke-and-heal.
implementation_plan: Phase 1: Controller core + API porting (2 wks) - scaffold a controller service that accepts recommended config bundles and persists rollout state. Phase 2: Canary engine (2 wks) - implement percentage ramp, simulated dry-run traffic harness, and telemetry diff checks. Phase 3: Guardrails and rollback (1 wk) - implement choke logic, fast revert wiring to runtime router, and audit events. Phase 4: Console integration and approvals (1 wk) - UI for checkpoints and one-click rollbacks/approvals. Phase 5: On-call runbook, tests and soft launch (1 wk). Implementation notes: use existing rollout-state table in config-store, reuse telemetry evaluator from optimize-suggester, and add small runtime hook to apply/revert batching cache configs via the serving runtime's config API.
rollout_plan: Start with internal pilot tenants: 5% of traffic for 24h -> 25% for 6h -> 100% for 1h (only after green checks). For external customers opt-in via a 'pilot' flag; require explicit customer opt-in and notify SRE/CS. Default gating thresholds: p95 latency delta <= +10ms, server_error_rate delta <= +0.05%, token_throughput >= +3%, quality delta on eval set (ROUGE/Cohere-sim) <= -0.5% relative. If any threshold breached, choke immediately, revert latest step, and notify operator channel #sre-optimize. Use canary windows that sample deterministic request hashes to ensure stable comparison groups.
monitoring_playbook: Signals to monitor: p50/p95 latency, cpu/gpu utilization, server_error_rate (5xx), K/V cache hit ratio, prefix_cache_miss_cost, token_throughput, sample-based quality checks against golden prompt-set. Alerts: - Immediate P0 alert if server_error_rate increases >0.2% absolute or p95 increases >100ms. - P1 alert for sustained degradation across 3 windows. Runbook steps: 1) Pause rollout via controller UI. 2) Trigger automated rollback (controller endpoint) and verify runtime reverted. 3) Collect debug traces (trace-id window, model KV stats, kernel selection logs). 4) If rollback fails, fail open to known stable variant and page on-call. Dashboard links: https://console.redwood.com/dashboards/optimize/choke-and-heal and GitHub PRs will reference the controller repo.
test_plan: Unit tests for controller state transitions, integration tests for apply/revert paths using a local runtime staging harness, canary simulation tests with synthetic traffic generator, and end-to-end smoke tests with a small internal tenant. Create an automated chaos test that flips a canary threshold mid-rollout to validate choke-heal behavior. Tests must be runnable in CI under 'optimize-autodeploy' pipeline. Add a postmortem checklist to ensure telemetry coverage in canary windows.
